text:
Beckett Sennecke went third overall in 2024 to raised eyebrows, and he's making the Ducks look smart. He's 20, playing over 20 minutes a night (up from 17 and a half as a rookie), and on the top power play, which he's on for 82% of the time compared with 47% last season. That's 23 points in 19 games, 10 goals, and a five-game point streak.

The role is real. The numbers on top of it are running hot. He's shooting 21% against a talent range near 14%, and Anaheim has scored 14.4 more goals than expected with him on the ice, among the biggest on-ice luck figures we have. At five on five the Ducks are under water in expected goals with him out there, though a little better than without him.

The tools are clear. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 94th percentile among forwards for chances from the slot last season. Forwards picked in the top five usually manage about half a point a game in their first full season. He's at 1.21. Expect that to slow, not stop.
headline: Sennecke's second season is off and running
